One glossary for every year of the course. The words you need in MYP1 are here, and so are the ones DP students use for
their portfolios and for TOK. Pick your year to see only what applies to you. Click a term to open it, and copy the link to
share a filtered list. Click any heading to fold its section.

## TOK connections

Questions that join a music word to one of the twelve TOK concepts. The ones marked *DP guide* are the DP Music guide's own
list of TOK questions for music students (p. 9); the others were written for this course. Use them for TOK discussions,
exhibition objects, or to push a DP reflection further.

::: {.crs}
<div id="gl-tokgrid" class="gl-tokgrid"></div>
:::

## Command term ladders

The verb in a rubric tells you what kind of thinking earns the marks. In the MYP the top-band verb climbs each stage: what
earned 7–8 in MYP1 earns 5–6 in MYP2. See the [pathway](pathway.qmd) for what that means in each unit.

::: {.crs}
<div id="gl-ladders"></div>
:::

## About this glossary

- **Where the words come from.** Music vocabulary from the class music dictionary; MYP key and related concepts and command terms from
  the MYP Arts guide; DP terms and assessment terms from the DP Music guide (first assessment 2022); TOK terms from the TOK course
  glossary; Music Learning Theory terms from Gordon's *Learning Sequences in Music*. Each term names its source.
- **The DP course is changing.** A new DP Music course starts in fall 2028. The DP terms here are for the current course; the new one
  will be added when its guide is out.
- **"In class" dates** come from the class site ([classes.seancoleman.org](https://classes.seancoleman.org)): each lesson page that uses a
  term is listed under it, oldest first.
- **For the teacher.** Edit `course/glossary.org`, then run `node scripts/course-glossary.mjs`.

Gordon, Edwin E. *Learning Sequences in Music: A Contemporary Music Learning Theory*. 2012 ed., GIA Publications, 2012. Skill learning sequence: partial synthesis (pp. 111–117), the verbal association warning (p. 108), generalization-aural/oral and -verbal (pp. 131–133); same is easier to hear than different (p. 219); tonal and rhythm patterns kept apart (p. 223); rhythm patterns chanted with vocal inflection like speech (p. 101); macrobeats stressed, not accented, and approached with a decrescendo, expression found between macrobeats, anacruses given special attention, weight and flow, displaced energy in rests and long durations (pp. 187–190).; Theory Concepts pages: Keyality versus key signature (p. xiii); tonality "best refers to what is usually called a mode," the eight tonalities (p. 149); movable-do with la-based minor and the rhythm syllables du de, du da di (p. 105); resting tone and tonic, a tonality in any keyality (p. 150); unitonal and multitonal music (pp. 152, 157); usual duple, triple and combined meter (pp. 175–176); no direct relation between measure signatures and meter, 6/8 as "duple compound" called inaccurate (p. 176); accents and microbeat divisions do not make meter (pp. 176–177); unusual meter, paired and unpaired, intact, macrobeats versus microbeats establishing meter (pp. 179–180).; Course pages (glossary, enrichment): audiation defined and compared with imitation (Introduction; pp. 3, 9); notation as a window (p. 8); patterns as units of meaning (pp. 99–100); the aural/oral level and the pause (pp. 101–102); discrimination and inference learning, theory delayed (p. 106); levels of the skill learning sequence (from pp. 111, 117, 126, 129, 136, 141); stepwise and bridging movement, Table 17 (pp. 230–231).

International Baccalaureate Organization. *Diploma Programme Music Guide*. First assessment 2022, International Baccalaureate Organization, 2020. Music and theory of knowledge, the TOK questions quoted on the glossary (p. 9); the four areas of inquiry and their example genres (pp. 22–23); personal, local and global contexts (pp. 23–24); musical processes and components (p. 24); musical roles of researcher, creator and performer (p. 25); the contemporary music-maker, artistic vision and collaboration (p. 37); assessment outline and weightings (pp. 42–43); achievement levels and assessment terms, with definitions (pp. 71–73).

International Baccalaureate Organization. *MYP Arts Guide*. For use from September 2022/January 2023, International Baccalaureate Organization. Key concepts and arts related concepts with their arts elaborations (as collected on the MYP concepts site); the command terms and their definitions, as quoted in the course's task-sheet notes (page numbers not checked); the Year 1, 3 and 5 assessment criteria behind the pathway's rubric tables (pp. 39–46). Publication year not printed in the excerpt held.
